newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to get investment rating in 98 - Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to get investment rating in 98 - Morgan.

text.p: The Philippines may not get an investment grade rating from international credit rating agencies until after the election of a new president next year, investment bank Morgan Stanley said on Friday.

The Philippines' sovereign rating is currently at Ba2, two notches below investment grade. Moody's Investors Service said last month it was reviewing the rating for a possible upgrade because of the successful implementation of policies, particularly in fiscal reform.
Morgan Stanley analyst Khalid Azam said in a report that the the Philippines will likely receive a one notch credit upgrade this year.

"Though we believe the numbers in the Philippines are compelling enough to warrant an investment grade rating, the rating agenices are unlikely to move the rating two notches, particularly in an election year," he said.

"Rather we feel that the rating agencies will wait until after elections to see the agenda of a new presidential administration. However, we do believe the Philippines is likely to be investment grade in 1998," he added.
The Philippines holds its next presidential elections in May 1998.
Azam said the recent passage of a tax reform bill had laid to rest doubts on the Philippines' fiscal surplus position.
Also, the nation's export growth, at an average of 16.8 percent in volumes the past five years, had brought it closer to the status of its Asian tiger neighbours, he said.
